# Test fixtures

## Provenance

Every fixture here is **synthetic**. No real resume, no real person, no real PII. Names,
emails, phone numbers and employers are invented; any resemblance to a real record is
coincidental.

## How PDFs are made

Generated by `scripts/make-fixtures.ts` (via `scripts/lib/pdf-builder.ts`, a hand-rolled
minimal PDF writer) and **committed as binaries**.

Regenerate with:

```bash
pnpm fixtures
```

Then review the diff and commit.

### Why they are committed rather than generated at test time

Generating PDFs inside `beforeAll` with jsPDF or pdfkit makes every test hostage to that
library's version and to whichever fonts happen to exist on the CI runner — the opposite of
deterministic. The writer is hand-rolled for the same reason: no dependency can silently
change the bytes under us.

## What each PDF pins

Each fixture exists to hold a specific layout heuristic in place. Deleting one silently
removes a guard.

| Fixture                    | Pins                                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `single-column-clean`      | Happy path. `hasMultipleColumns` false, full structure detected                      |
| `two-column-true`          | A real 0.3in gutter — **must** be detected. PRD §5.3's literal >150px rule misses it |
| `right-aligned-dates`      | Single column with dates flushed right — **must not** false-positive as 2 columns    |
| `skills-three-column-list` | One table-like line only — must **not** set `hasTables`                              |
| `three-line-stub`          | The §8.2 low anchor. Zero bullets: the input that produced `NaN` (ADR 0001 §4)       |
| `scanned-image-only`       | No text layer → specific `NO_TEXT_LAYER` error, not a silent zero score              |
| `with-logo-image`          | Image above the 50-unit threshold → `hasImages` true                                 |
| `glyph-only-image`         | Image below the threshold → `hasImages` false                                        |
| `three-page`               | Page-count penalty and the Workday truncation quirk                                  |
| `small-font-tight-leading` | 8pt on 9.6pt leading — breaks a fixed 3px y-tolerance                                |
| `ligatures-unicode`        | Ligatures and non-ASCII names survive normalisation                                  |
| `all-caps-headers`         | Eight ALL-CAPS headers: good ATS practice vs PRD §7.4's uncapped penalty             |

## Expected outputs

`expected/parse/*.json` and `expected/score/*.json` are golden files. They are
human-reviewed; a diff in a PR means behaviour changed and someone must confirm the change
was intended.

Score goldens are deliberately **not** committed until the Phase 3 calibration pass — before
then every stub-swap would rewrite them and reviewers would stop reading the diffs.
